subject.title: fix stale app-state recovery for chat writes

question: Should this persistence and schema-changing recovery path require a successful redacted real recovery run on the final rebased head before merge, rather than relying on historical success proof plus exact-head failure-safe evidence?
rationale: The branch deliberately changed the recovery architecture after the successful eed6914 run, and provider disconnects prevented equivalent success proof for the later design; accepting that gap is a release-risk judgment.

options.title: Require final-head recovery proof
options.body: Rebase first, then require a redacted successful archive, mute, or equivalent stale-store recovery run that demonstrates the final persistence design before merging.

options.title: Accept failure-safe evidence
options.body: Merge after conflict resolution based on focused tests and the retained-debt failure path, accepting that the final architecture lacks a successful live recovery run.

recommendation.title: Require final-head recovery proof
recommendation.body: Rebase first, then require a redacted successful archive, mute, or equivalent stale-store recovery run that demonstrates the final persistence design before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the recovery redesign and documented the exact-head failure-safe validation constraints.
